chapter: Billy and De De Pierce, Al Hirt tour
title: On the road with Al Hirt's show
summary: Describes a show with Hirt that combined brass bands and small bands, and a trip with long travel.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: We only got a few more minutes if you can make it. I'll make it. Looks like about seven, five minutes, something like that. You mentioned something about Al Hurd. How did that work?

That was nice, man. I enjoyed winning Chucks with him. He was all right, man. He's a pretty good fella, too. It was really something that I enjoyed. When we were going on the road with him, he would come on stage with his group. Then after they grew, then we would come on with a small band, a seven-piece band. Then after we get off the stage, then Contra would come on with a small seven-piece band. Then Hoist, he would come back and when the ending of the show, he would pick up Clothes of Walker Peek and Divi Ramblin. Then one band would come in, big brass band would come in, one on his side and one on that side. Then they'd march all in together until we get to the bandstand. You understand, we all joined together. Then he would close with the Saints. And Ed O. Emma Thomas, when she was singing with the Contra, and every way he went, he made a hit with it. Some of us had gone to Nevada one time, Reno, but the deal fell true. They'd take the whole thirty-six positions to make that. But I don't know, the deal fell true.
With Marty. You were with Marty.
And he had a seven-piece band like a dancer?

We'd take seven out of the brass band. Oh, I see. So he'd pick seven out of the brass band. Al would tell you who we'd pick out the brass band. And we'd take seven out of each band, and make a short band. Then at the end, we'd all get together and play together.

But when we used a small band he would play clarinet also. But in a big band he'd play clarinet. But the sad part, one trip I think we went to play one night in May, St. George, and the next night we played in Atlanta. Well, how of them had gigs here they couldn't make that. They said, well, I was caught up. He said, how of them over there? Boy, I always said, no, never no more. Never no more. He'd want them back no more. That was nice to work with them, man.
I wonder why he didn't like them.

They couldn't play for her and go out and sing. She always did her sing with Contra. Blast off us. She thought maybe she'd sing with them. If she did better, she sang with us. But if she'd sing with us, she'd sing with Howard. And they couldn't play our numbers. And Albert Walters was with us. He had to go join them to get the band on the right foot.
